Details needed for a quotation

Download order acceptance checklist
Drawing and acceptance requirements
Send a consistent drawing package

Include a 3D model, such as STEP, and a 2D drawing when dimensions, fits or surface requirements are not fully defined in the model. Label the part number and units, and identify the drawing revision. If the files disagree, identify which document controls before requesting a quotation.

For multi-axis parts, include the overall envelope, stock dimensions and part weight where known so tool access and setup can be reviewed.

Working from a sample

If you have a sample without a drawing, describe the known requirements. Ask which measurements or design work are needed to define the part. A sample alone cannot establish hidden material or treatment requirements.

Mark the dimensions used for acceptance

Identify mating bores and shaft fits on the drawing, with their datums and tolerances. Mark sealing faces, threads and any other critical features too. State whether dimensions apply before or after finishing.

If you need a particular inspection record, send the format or an example with your inquiry. Agree the inspection and documentation requirements before ordering. Ask LZZ to confirm the measurement method and instrument range, then request calibration evidence and confirmation that your required project records are available.

Inspection & documentation requirements
Specify the material and final surface
Material requirements

State the exact alloy or polymer grade, or the functional requirement if selection is still open. Include any required material documentation and whether substitutes may be considered.

Finish and surface requirements

Provide the finish specification and appearance requirements. State whether acceptance dimensions apply before or after finishing. Mark cosmetic faces and masked areas, and define edge conditions. Include customer or industry standards and certificates required for this part or program, stating each standard, revision and scope.

Drawing and quotation
1. Define part requirements

Send your drawing or model with its revision and the material grade. Include the quantity and required delivery date, and describe the part function.

If you are working from a sample, explain the fit and function to retain or change. Identify any material changes, then agree the measurement and drawing work needed to define the part.

2. Review the quotation

Check that the quotation uses the correct drawing revision. Discuss tool access and workholding with the team, and approve any proposed geometry changes against the mating features and critical dimensions.

Prepare the drawing and order inputs
QUOTATION SCOPE
Machining & material
Drawing revision, grade, quantity, price and any agreed alternative.
Surface finishing
Included treatments and the surfaces to be controlled.
Inspection
Report scope, sampling and required records.
Separate charges
Tooling, special documentation, freight and duties where applicable.
Delivery terms
Production timing, shipping arrangements and responsibilities.
Payment and sample charges

Before accepting a quote or placing an order, confirm the payment method and currency. Agree the payment stages and the amount due at each stage.

For sample work, ask about machining and setup charges. Confirm sample freight and whether any sample fee can be credited to a later order.

Approve before production
3. Check and approve the sample

Set the sample acceptance criteria before machining. Identify critical interfaces and appearance requirements, with any functional tests needed.

Set the first-article review stage and release criteria. Record the drawing revision and approval criteria before moving to production.

Release the specification for repeat orders
4. Agree on batch inspection

Confirm the approved revision and checks for repeat production. Identify the features that need recorded results.

Agree material traceability requirements and the treatment of nonconforming parts. Our quality planning guide covers the records to request.

View quality planning guide
Packing and delivery documents
Protected machined parts · LZZ packing archive, November 2022
5. Arrange packing and shipment

The parts and shipment requirements determine whether cartons or wooden cases are used. Identify polished faces and sealing surfaces that need protection, along with vulnerable threads.

Specify the labels and part numbers required. Include the drawing revision and quantity per pack where needed. Provide the delivery address and receiving contact.

Separate the required arrival date from the dispatch date. Confirm the shipping method, Incoterm, packing protection, transport costs and responsibility for customs, duties and taxes in the quotation. Any arrival-date commitment must also be agreed.

6. Confirm documents for delivery

Use the approved drawing revision and order reference consistently for packing, shipment and inspection documents.

Specify the records needed with delivery, such as an agreed dimensional report or material documentation.

Resources
Frequently asked questions
Custom CNC machining FAQ
Essential answers
What is the minimum order quantity?

Orders start at 1 piece. Include the first-order quantity and expected repeat demand so we can quote prototype work and later batches separately.

Planning prototypes and repeat batches
What is the production lead time?

Production takes 7-14 business days after drawing and order confirmation, including surface finishing. Shipping time is additional. Record the confirmed production schedule and delivery arrangements in your quotation and order.

How to order
What should I send for a quotation?

Send the drawing revision, units, material grade, finish, quantity and delivery destination. Include a STEP model where available and a dimensioned 2D drawing identifying critical tolerances, threads and acceptance requirements.

Drawing and RFQ checklist
Does the website send my inquiry or upload my drawing?

The form creates an email draft without uploading files or sending a request. Open the draft in your email app, attach the drawings and send it to LZZ. You can also copy the draft or save it as a text file.

Prepare an inquiry
Quotes, payment, samples & after-sales
Which payment terms should I confirm?

Before accepting a quote or placing an order, ask LZZ to confirm the payment method and currency. Agree the payment stages and the amount due at each stage for that order.

Payment and order terms
How are samples charged?

Ask for the sample machining and setup charges before approving the work. Confirm the sample freight cost and whether any sample fee can be credited to a later order.

Sample charges to confirm
Which after-sales terms apply to my parts?

Agree the terms for the quoted part before ordering. Confirm any warranty period and start date, exclusions and the procedure for reporting a problem. Ask who covers rework or replacement, return freight and any agreed refund.

After-sales terms to confirm
How do I report a nonconforming part?

Send the drawing revision and part or batch reference, then include the affected quantity, photographs and measurement details. LZZ reviews the discrepancy against the agreed acceptance criteria and agrees corrective action with you.

Nonconforming-part review
Processes & specifications
Which machining services can I discuss with LZZ?

We offer CNC milling and turning, with five-axis machining for suitable geometry. Plastic machining and finish machining of castings are also available. Send the complete drawing so we can plan the setup and finish; for castings, identify who supplies and accepts the blank.

Explore the five machining services
How should I specify the material and finish?

Specify the exact material grade and condition. A broad label such as aluminum, steel or plastic leaves the grade undefined. Identify cosmetic faces and surface treatment requirements, then mark masked areas and dimensions to check after finishing. Record the agreed specification in the quotation.

Material and finish guide
Can every feature hold ±0.01 mm?

No. ±0.01 mm is a conditional reference for selected critical features. The achievable limit depends on material and geometry, together with the setup and measurement method. Mark each critical tolerance on the drawing for confirmation.

Tolerance review and quality control
Inspection & delivery
Which inspection documents should I request?

Specify the dimensional results and first-article records you need before ordering. Include material traceability and finishing documents where required. Agree the features and sampling plan, then confirm the report format. The quotation records the included document package and any additional cost; request current calibration evidence separately where needed.

Inspection and delivery documents
Is LZZ ISO 9001 certified?

LZZ is ISO 9001 certified. For supplier qualification, request the current certificate for Hangzhou Lizhizao Precision Machinery Co., Ltd., including its number, issuer, validity, scope and verification details. Company awards are separate from the ISO certificate, and quality-system certification does not replace part-specific acceptance or industry approval.

Request supplier qualification documents
How are packing and international shipping agreed?

Provide the destination, receiving requirements and any vulnerable or cosmetic surfaces that need protection. Confirm the packing method, transport method, trade term and named place in the quotation. Agree the packing list, commercial invoice and other required documents. Transit time is separate from production time.

Shipment planning checklist
Machining studies
What do the machining studies show?

The studies use workshop photographs to explain part features and machining setups. They outline drawing requirements for a similar part, without publishing customer inspection or performance results.

Manufacturing guide
Define part requirements before machining
Identify the working surfaces

A housing or shaft is located by the surfaces that meet other parts. Mark those interfaces on the drawing, including surfaces used to seal, slide or carry load. For a mounting block, identify the locating faces so tolerances can be assessed against the assembly function.

Compare milled pockets and housings with turned shafts and fittings. Some designs need both operations; the geometry determines the process choice.

Specify critical dimensions

Give critical features their datums and acceptance limits. A 3D model defines shape, but a controlled 2D drawing may also be needed to specify fits and surface texture. Include edge conditions and measurement requirements where they affect acceptance.

Tolerances are assessed for each drawing. Achievable limits depend on the material and feature geometry, together with the setup and measurement method. Agree on inspection requirements and supporting records for your design.

Specify material and surface requirements

State the exact alloy or plastic grade, material condition and any material-certificate requirement. For coated parts, specify the finish and whether critical dimensions apply before or after treatment. Mark areas that need masking, cosmetic faces and burr-sensitive edges.

Name the applicable standards and their revisions. Include traceability and approval requirements, with the intended end use and any export requirements. The material and finish checklist covers the detailed fields.

Define acceptance checks and revisions

Define the checks needed to accept the part, whether they concern assembly fit, appearance or a functional test. Set the criteria before machining. For a design change, issue a revised drawing identifying the affected features.

Record the controlled drawing revision, material, finish and approval criteria. Sample approval does not cover a changed design or material. Prototype-to-repeat planning explains how to release the approved specification; How we work covers the order approval.

Resources
Process comparison
Choosing CNC milling, turning or 5-axis machining

A shaft or sleeve will usually start with turning. A housing with pockets and flat mounting faces is more likely to need milling. Angled features or access to several faces may call for a multi-axis setup. Some parts need a combination; send the drawing so we can review the sequence.

Compare the processes by geometry
Process	Typical geometry	Drawing requirements
CNC turning	Rotational features such as a shaft, sleeve, disc or fitting, often arranged around an axis. Turning capabilities.	Define the datum axis, diameters, shoulders, grooves, threads and runout if required. Confirm whether cross-holes, flats or slots need secondary milling.
CNC milling	Block-like or irregular forms with pockets, slots, holes, contours and planar mounting faces. Milling capabilities.	Define datum faces, pocket depth, hole patterns and positional relationships. Confirm stock, clamping surfaces, setups and inspection records.
Multi-axis machining	Features distributed over several faces, angled faces or areas that need different tool approaches. Multi-axis capabilities.	Define common datums, face-to-face and angular relationships. Review tool access, workholding and sequence against the model.
Parts that need more than one process
CNC turning operation.
CNC milling operation.
Five-axis machining operation.

Some turned parts also need milling, for example to add flats or cross-holes. A housing may require another setup to reach an angled face. The machining sequence must preserve the relationships between critical features, so send both a 3D model and the controlling 2D drawing.

Accuracy depends on the feature

Accuracy is assessed at the feature level. Geometry and material affect the achievable limit, together with the setup and datum strategy. Finishing and the measurement method also affect acceptance. State the tolerance and datum for each critical interface so its machining and inspection can be planned.

Files for a process recommendation
A 3D model and the controlling 2D drawing revision.
Material grade and condition, or the functional requirement if still undecided.
Quantity for the first order and expected repeat pattern, if known.
Critical datums, fits, surface requirements and required inspection records.
Finish, packaging and required arrival date, with any standards or approvals identified.

Use the RFQ checklist to organize those details. We review your drawing before confirming the machining process and quoting a price and schedule.

mainText:
Resources
Design preparation
Specifying material and finish for a machined part
Confirm the material specification

State the exact alloy or polymer grade and condition, with the applicable standard. Include the certificates and traceability records required. If substitutes may be considered, identify them for approval and confirm the material documents in the quotation.

Describe the part function and mating assembly. Include loads and operating temperature, with exposure or electrical requirements where relevant. Specify any cleanliness, chemical-contact or ESD limits and the evidence needed for acceptance. If the grade is undecided, send these conditions for engineering review..

Related part examples

Examples with related features. Each custom part is quoted to its own drawing.

Billet aluminum engine covers
Functional plastic blocks & structures
Next step

Use the RFQ checklist to prepare your drawing and order details.

View RFQ checklist
Compare materials against the part requirements

The catalog groups parts as aluminum, stainless steel, copper and brass, and engineering plastics. The grades below are examples for selection, rather than a stock list. Properties depend on the grade and condition. Suitability and availability are confirmed for the part and proposed finish in the quotation.

Material family	Brochure examples	Selection questions
Aluminum	6061, 7075, 2024	Compare strength, stiffness, part mass, environment and finish needs. Specify the exact alloy and temper.
Stainless steel	304, 316, 17-4PH	Compare the service environment and mechanical requirements. Specify the grade, condition and any required heat treatment.
Copper / brass	See the material naming note below.	Define the electrical or thermal role and service environment. Confirm the exact designation and applicable standard.
Engineering plastics	POM, PEEK, PPSU	Compare temperature, load, chemical exposure, electrical behavior and mating material. Specify the polymer grade and condition.
Other named materials	Titanium, Inconel, Kovar, Invar	Provide the exact material designation and intended use for engineering review.
Confirm the alloy designation

The original brochure names C3600 and H62, while the supplied material sheet lists C36000 brass. Their equivalence is not established. Confirm the exact designation and applicable standard in your inquiry.

Define the finish and acceptance criteria

Finishing options depend on the material. Services include deburring and polishing, with blasting, anodizing, passivation or plating where suitable. The quotation confirms the treatment and supporting documents for your part.

Process specification: identify the material and treatment, including the finish standard and revision where applicable. Specify controlled color, gloss, texture, coating thickness or roughness; separate visual appearance from the finish's function.
Faces and edges: mark cosmetic faces and specify edge breaks and deburring or polishing requirements. For bead blasting, agree the appearance and whether a reference sample is needed.
Masking and function: mark protected threads, mating bores and other interfaces, plus surfaces for corrosion protection, electrical contact or sealing. For anodizing, confirm the alloy, color and coating requirements. For passivation or plating, confirm the process specification and protected areas.
Dimensions and inspection: state whether acceptance dimensions apply before or after treatment. Critical dimensions are checked at the agreed stage, including after finishing where required.
Order records: specify the material and treatment documents and acceptance records required. We link the requested documents to the relevant part or batch reference.
Requirement	Specification	Inspection stage
Substrate	Exact material grade and condition.	Confirm before treatment.
Treatment	Required coating or treatment, standard and revision.	Agree process before production.
Coat or mask	Faces, bores, threads and interfaces to coat or protect.	Identify before treatment; verify agreed interfaces after treatment.
Critical dimensions	Whether acceptance dimensions apply before or after coating.	Check at the specified stage.
Thickness	Coating thickness requirements and the agreed measurement method.	Agree any required after-treatment check and record.
Appearance	Cosmetic faces, color, gloss, texture and any agreed reference.	Agree appearance criteria before work; review the finished part.
Tests and records	Required tests, limits, sampling, document format and part or batch reference.	Confirm availability and scope in the quotation; record agreed results.

See the original surface-coating photographs and agree order documentation.

Use the finish specification and inspection criteria to accept the part.

Record the requirements in your RFQ

Record the material and finish on the controlled drawing or specification. Include inspection and traceability requirements in your RFQ package, using the quality checklist to check the details before you prepare an inquiry.

Send a consistent drawing package

Working from a sample

Mark the dimensions used for acceptance

Identify mating bores and shaft fits on the drawing, with their datums and tolerances. Mark sealing faces, threads and any other critical features too. State whether dimensions apply before or after finishing.

If you need a particular inspection record, send the format or an example with your inquiry. Agree the inspection and documentation requirements before ordering. Frequently asked questions
Custom CNC machining FAQ
Essential answers
What is the minimum order quantity?

Orders start at 1 piece. Include the first-order quantity and expected repeat demand so we can quote prototype work and later batches separately.

Planning prototypes and repeat batches
What is the production lead time?

Production takes 7-14 business days after drawing and order confirmation, including surface finishing. Shipping time is additional. Record the confirmed production schedule and delivery arrangements in your quotation and order.

How to order
What should I send for a quotation?

Send the drawing revision, units, material grade, finish, quantity and delivery destination. Include a STEP model where available and a dimensioned 2D drawing identifying critical tolerances, threads and acceptance requirements.

Drawing and RFQ checklist
Does the website send my inquiry or upload my drawing?

The form creates an email draft without uploading files or sending a request. Open the draft in your email app, attach the drawings and send it to LZZ. You can also copy the draft or save it as a text file.

Prepare an inquiry
Quotes, payment, samples & after-sales
Which payment terms should I confirm?

Before accepting a quote or placing an order, ask LZZ to confirm the payment method and currency. Agree the payment stages and the amount due at each stage for that order.

Payment and order terms
How are samples charged?

Ask for the sample machining and setup charges before approving the work. Confirm the sample freight cost and whether any sample fee can be credited to a later order.

Sample charges to confirm
Which after-sales terms apply to my parts?

Agree the terms for the quoted part before ordering. Confirm any warranty period and start date, exclusions and the procedure for reporting a problem. Ask who covers rework or replacement, return freight and any agreed refund.

After-sales terms to confirm
How do I report a nonconforming part?

Send the drawing revision and part or batch reference, then include the affected quantity, photographs and measurement details. LZZ reviews the discrepancy against the agreed acceptance criteria and agrees corrective action with you.

Nonconforming-part review
Processes & specifications
Which machining services can I discuss with LZZ?

We offer CNC milling and turning, with five-axis machining for suitable geometry. Plastic machining and finish machining of castings are also available. Send the complete drawing so we can plan the setup and finish; for castings, identify who supplies and accepts the blank.

Explore the five machining services
How should I specify the material and finish?

Specify the exact material grade and condition. A broad label such as aluminum, steel or plastic leaves the grade undefined. Identify cosmetic faces and surface treatment requirements, then mark masked areas and dimensions to check after finishing. Record the agreed specification in the quotation.

Material and finish guide
Can every feature hold ±0.01 mm?

No. ±0.01 mm is a conditional reference for selected critical features. The achievable limit depends on material and geometry, together with the setup and measurement method. Mark each critical tolerance on the drawing for confirmation.

Tolerance review and quality control
Inspection & delivery
Which inspection documents should I request?

Specify the dimensional results and first-article records you need before ordering. Include material traceability and finishing documents where required. Agree the features and sampling plan, then confirm the report format. The quotation records the included document package and any additional cost; request current calibration evidence separately where needed.

Inspection and delivery documents
Is LZZ ISO 9001 certified?

LZZ is ISO 9001 certified. For supplier qualification, request the current certificate for Hangzhou Lizhizao Precision Machinery Co., Ltd., including its number, issuer, validity, scope and verification details. Company awards are separate from the ISO certificate, and quality-system certification does not replace part-specific acceptance or industry approval.

Request supplier qualification documents
How are packing and international shipping agreed?

Provide the destination, receiving requirements and any vulnerable or cosmetic surfaces that need protection. Confirm the packing method, transport method, trade term and named place in the quotation. Agree the packing list, commercial invoice and other required documents. Transit time is separate from production time.

Shipment planning checklist

What do the machining studies show?

The studies use workshop photographs to explain part features and machining setups. They outline drawing requirements for a similar part, without publishing customer inspection or performance results.

Identify the working surfaces

A housing or shaft is located by the surfaces that meet other parts. Mark those interfaces on the drawing, including surfaces used to seal, slide or carry load. For a mounting block, identify the locating faces so tolerances can be assessed against the assembly function.

Compare milled pockets and housings with turned shafts and fittings. Some designs need both operations; the geometry determines the process choice.

Specify critical dimensions

Give critical features their datums and acceptance limits. A 3D model defines shape, but a controlled 2D drawing may also be needed to specify fits and surface texture. Include edge conditions and measurement requirements where they affect acceptance.

Tolerances are assessed for each drawing. Achievable limits depend on the material and feature geometry, together with the setup and measurement method. Agree on inspection requirements and supporting records for your design.

mainText:
Resources
Process comparison
Choosing CNC milling, turning or 5-axis machining

A shaft or sleeve will usually start with turning. A housing with pockets and flat mounting faces is more likely to need milling. Angled features or access to several faces may call for a multi-axis setup. Some parts need a combination; send the drawing so we can review the sequence.

Compare the processes by geometry
CNC turning
Typical geometry

Rotational features such as a shaft, sleeve, disc or fitting, often arranged around an axis. Turning capabilities.

Drawing requirements

Define the datum axis, diameters, shoulders, grooves, threads and runout if required. Confirm whether cross-holes, flats or slots need secondary milling.

CNC milling
Typical geometry

Block-like or irregular forms with pockets, slots, holes, contours and planar mounting faces. Milling capabilities.

Drawing requirements

Define datum faces, pocket depth, hole patterns and positional relationships. Confirm stock, clamping surfaces, setups and inspection records.

Multi-axis machining
Typical geometry

Features distributed over several faces, angled faces or areas that need different tool approaches. Multi-axis capabilities.

Drawing requirements

Define common datums, face-to-face and angular relationships. Review tool access, workholding and sequence against the model.

Parts that need more than one process
CNC turning operation.
CNC milling operation.
Five-axis machining operation.

Some turned parts also need milling, for example to add flats or cross-holes. A housing may require another setup to reach an angled face. The machining sequence must preserve the relationships between critical features, so send both a 3D model and the controlling 2D drawing.

Accuracy depends on the feature

Accuracy is assessed at the feature level. Geometry and material affect the achievable limit, together with the setup and datum strategy. Finishing and the measurement method also affect acceptance. State the tolerance and datum for each critical interface so its machining and inspection can be planned.

Files for a process recommendation
A 3D model and the controlling 2D drawing revision.
Material grade and condition, or the functional requirement if still undecided.
Quantity for the first order and expected repeat pattern, if known.
Critical datums, fits, surface requirements and required inspection records.
Finish, packaging and required arrival date, with any standards or approvals identified.

Design preparation
Specifying material and finish for a machined part
Confirm the material specification

State the exact alloy or polymer grade and condition, with the applicable standard. Include the certificates and traceability records required. If substitutes may be considered, identify them for approval and confirm the material documents in the quotation.

Describe the part function and mating assembly. Include loads and operating temperature, with exposure or electrical requirements where relevant. Specify any cleanliness, chemical-contact or ESD limits and the evidence needed for acceptance. If the grade is undecided, send these conditions for engineering review..

Related part examples

Functional plastic blocks & structures

View RFQ checklist
Compare materials against the part requirements

The catalog groups parts as aluminum, stainless steel, copper and brass, and engineering plastics. The grades below are examples for selection, rather than a stock list. Properties depend on the grade and condition. Suitability and availability are confirmed for the part and proposed finish in the quotation.

Aluminum
Brochure examples

6061, 7075, 2024

Selection questions

Compare strength, stiffness, part mass, environment and finish needs. Specify the exact alloy and temper.

Stainless steel
Brochure examples

304, 316, 17-4PH

Selection questions

Compare the service environment and mechanical requirements. Specify the grade, condition and any required heat treatment.

Copper / brass
Brochure examples

See the material naming note below.

Selection questions

Define the electrical or thermal role and service environment. Confirm the exact designation and applicable standard.

Engineering plastics
Brochure examples

POM, PEEK, PPSU

Selection questions

Compare temperature, load, chemical exposure, electrical behavior and mating material. Specify the polymer grade and condition.

Other named materials
Brochure examples

Titanium, Inconel, Kovar, Invar

Selection questions

Provide the exact material designation and intended use for engineering review.

Confirm the alloy designation

The original brochure names C3600 and H62, while the supplied material sheet lists C36000 brass. Their equivalence is not established. Confirm the exact designation and applicable standard in your inquiry.

Define the finish and acceptance criteria

Finishing options depend on the material. Services include deburring and polishing, with blasting, anodizing, passivation or plating where suitable. The quotation confirms the treatment and supporting documents for your part.

Process specification: identify the material and treatment, including the finish standard and revision where applicable. Specify controlled color, gloss, texture, coating thickness or roughness; separate visual appearance from the finish's function.
Faces and edges: mark cosmetic faces and specify edge breaks and deburring or polishing requirements. For bead blasting, agree the appearance and whether a reference sample is needed.
Masking and function: mark protected threads, mating bores and other interfaces, plus surfaces for corrosion protection, electrical contact or sealing. For anodizing, confirm the alloy, color and coating requirements. For passivation or plating, confirm the process specification and protected areas.
Dimensions and inspection: state whether acceptance dimensions apply before or after treatment. Critical dimensions are checked at the agreed stage, including after finishing where required.
Order records: specify the material and treatment documents and acceptance records required. We link the requested documents to the relevant part or batch reference.

Packing and delivery requirements
Part protection
Information you provide

Mark cosmetic faces and sealing surfaces, then identify threads and fragile edges that need protection. State cleanliness and corrosion-protection needs. Specify pack weight or quantity limits and receiving-site handling requirements.

Confirm in the quotation

Agree protective materials, separation between parts and protection for threads and mating surfaces. Cartons or wooden cases depend on the part, quantity and transport route.

Pack identification
Information you provide

Part number, drawing revision, quantity per pack, batch identification and required labels.

Confirm in the quotation

Confirm available label, lot-reference and inspection-document formats. Use the same part and revision references on the packing list and agreed quality records.

Delivery basis
Information you provide

Full delivery address, receiving contact, required arrival date, requested trade term/version and named place.

Confirm in the quotation

Confirm who books transport and handles export/import clearance, insurance, duties, taxes and local delivery. EXW, FOB or DDP options are quoted for the applicable destination and service.

DDP applies only where included in the quotation.

Documents
Information you provide

The document list required by procurement, logistics or your destination-side import contact.

Confirm in the quotation

We provide protective packing with a packing list and commercial invoice, plus shipment information. Material and finishing records accompany the parts when specified in the order; the same applies to agreed dimensional records. Confirm which documents are available and who prepares each.

Schedule
Information you provide

Separate your required arrival date from the desired dispatch date.

Confirm in the quotation

Production takes 7-14 business days after drawing and order confirmation, including surface finishing. Transit is estimated separately and is not included in production time.

Transport options and import documents

Courier, air or sea arrangements depend on shipment size and destination. DHL, FedEx or UPS can be discussed when selecting a courier.

Agree additional customs documents before production with your importing entity or freight forwarder. Requirements depend on the destination and transaction.
